## What you should be able to do tonight

- Reproduce the size and value factor construction recipes from memory.
- State the risk-versus-alpha classification rule and apply it to a factor you have not thought about before.

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}

## Drill <span class='task-total'>interview thread</span>

Spaced repetition, not cramming. Every drill in the year is collected on the [drills page](../drills.qmd).

::: {.task-list .drill}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Arithmetic, timed, seventeenth sitting. Ten two-digit multiplications, the sevenths, and 45 times 45, 35 times 35 and 65 times 65 using the trick for numbers ending in 5.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Order statistics under a clock: n independent uniforms on the unit interval. What is the expected value of the maximum, the minimum, and the range? Then the expected gap between the largest and second largest, and what happens to it as n grows.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> The trading version: 20 traders each independently quote a price drawn from the same distribution, and you trade against the best quote. What is the expected quality of the price you get, and why does that make you cautious rather than pleased?
:::
:::
